scenes.narration: Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Death Stranding. Death Stranding is a 2019 action-adventure game written, produced, designed and directed by Hideo Kojima, developed by his company Kojima Productions and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment. It was first released for PlayStation 4 in November 2019, followed by a Windows port in July 2020.

The self that experiences Death Stranding is a committee, not a king. A director's cut was released for PlayStation 5 in September 2021, followed by releases for Windows in March 2022, iOS, iPadOS and macOS in January 2024, and Amazon Luna and Xbox Series X/S in November 2024. Sony published the game on their consoles, while 505 Games published all other versions under license from Kojima Productions.

Reproduction explains more of Death Stranding than any philosophy dares to admit. The game is set in the United States following a cataclysmic event which caused destructive creatures to begin roaming the Earth. The player controls Sam Porter Bridges (Norman Reedus), a courier tasked with delivering supplies to isolated colonies and reconnecting them via a wireless communications network.

Once you see Death Stranding as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. However, he is pursued by a genocidal militia group, led by a mysterious masked man known as Higgs, who intends to wipe out the remainder of humanity. Alongside Reedus, the game features actors Mads Mikkelsen, Léa Seydoux, Margaret Qualley, Troy Baker, Tommie Earl Jenkins, and Lindsay Wagner, in addition to the likenesses of film directors Guillermo del Toro and Nicolas Winding Refn, as supporting characters.

The story Death Stranding tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. Critics praised its voice acting, soundtrack, and visuals, with more mixed opinions regarding its gameplay and story. The game was nominated for several awards and won the most GOTY awards of any game in 2019.

Meaning is not found in Death Stranding — it is manufactured for it. As of March 2021, the game had sold 5 million copies worldwide. Numerous commentators later noted that elements of the game resembled the COVID-19 pandemic, which began during the months following its original release.

The cold light on Death Stranding leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. A sequel, Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, released on June 26, 2025, for PlayStation 5. Death Stranding is an action-adventure game set in an open world, and includes asynchronous online functions.

Death Stranding did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. Kojima refers to Death Stranding as the first "strand game", an original genre characterized by the game's incorporation of social elements. Kojima compared this genre to how his earlier game Metal Gear—now considered a stealth game—was called an action game during its release because the stealth genre had not been established.

The honest version of Death Stranding starts by giving up the comforting part. The player controls Sam Bridges, a porter for a company known as Bridges. The player is tasked with delivering supply cargo to various isolated cities known as Knots, as well as isolated researchers and survivalists, while also connecting them to a communications system known as the Chiral Network.

Strip Death Stranding of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. The player is evaluated by the company and recipients based on their performance (including via "likes" similar to social networks), including whether the cargo was delivered, and if it is intact, among other factors. These merits are, in turn, used to level up the player's statistics, such as stability and weight capacity, and increase their standing with individual locations and characters (which can improve rewards).

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Death Stranding shows exactly where that breaks. How cargo is packed by the player, and the overall weight being carried, affect Sam's ability to navigate through the environments. The game extensively uses licensed music, most often from the bands Silent Poets and Low Roar, to score and enhance specific set-pieces and moments of traversal.

What looks like free choice in Death Stranding is older than choice itself. The player's main enemies include otherworldly creatures known as "beached things" (BTs), MULEs (rogue, bandit-like porters obsessed with cargo, who attempt to steal and deliver it themselves), and Demens, MULEs who have begun killing porters to claim their cargo. BTs are surrounded by a rain known as "timefall", which damages the player's armor and cargo by speeding up their deterioration.

Nobody designed the part of Death Stranding you experience — it was inherited. BTs are normally invisible, but Sam's suit is equipped with a robotic sensor referred to in-game as an "odradek" that points towards nearby BTs, and the player can then scan the area to reveal them. As Sam is a "repatriate", he is taken to an underwater world known as the "Seam" if he is killed, where he can "swim" back to his body to revive himself.

Every serious account of Death Stranding eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. However, being killed and consumed by a BT results in a destructive explosion known as a "voidout", which permanently damages the location of the death with an untraversable crater. The Network is used as the basis for the game's online functionality, where players can leave supplies, structures, and messages that can be viewed and used by other players, although structures will eventually be destroyed by Timefall after some time.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Death Stranding — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. The player can recover cargo lost by other players to complete their delivery. BTs are created from the dead via necrosis, and when they consume a living human being, they create an explosion on the scale of a nuclear bomb, known as a "voidout".

The selfish-gene reading of Death Stranding makes it less romantic and far more precise. These events damaged the country's infrastructure, leading its remaining population to confine themselves to remote colonies known as "Knot Cities", which form the remaining "United Cities of America". These colonies have relied on the services of a company known as Bridges, whose porters brave the BTs, bandits, and terrorists to deliver supplies to the cities.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. If they achieve a mental connection to a "Bridge Baby" (a "BB")—a premature child reflecting a state between life and death—it is possible for a person to sense the presence of a BT. Porters carry a BB with them, stored in a pod simulating the womb of a "stillmother".

The feeling that Death Stranding means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. Depending on its severity, a condition known as "DOOMS" allows a person to naturally sense, see, or even control a BT, as well as granting a variety of powers, such as teleportation or travel to other people's Beaches. There are individuals known as "repatriates" who can travel back from "the Seam"—a place between the world of the living and the Beach—upon death.

Nothing in Death Stranding was built for you — it was built for reproduction. As such, these individuals can effectively return from death, though their deaths will still cause voidouts if killed during contact with a BT. Freelance courier Sam Porter Bridges (Norman Reedus) is transporting cargo to Central Knot City but is interrupted by Timefall and takes shelter.

The psychology underneath Death Stranding is simpler and older than the story on top. Sam arrives at his destination, where a citizen died by suicide, with the corpse on the verge of necrosis. Due to being both a repatriate and having DOOMS, Sam is given an emergency assignment to accompany the disposal team to an incinerator to dispose of the corpse.

Behind Death Stranding sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. However, an encounter with BTs causes a voidout that destroys Central Knot City. Sam revives in Capital Knot City and meets Deadman (Guillermo del Toro/Jesse Corti), a doctor from Bridges who has Sam deliver morphine to the dying President of the UCA: Sam's adoptive mother, Bridget Strand (Lindsay Wagner/Emily O'Brien).

The nihilist does not deny Death Stranding — he only refuses to flatter it. Bridget pleads with Sam to rejoin Bridges and help realize her dream of "reforming America" before succumbing to her illness. Sam takes her body for incineration but refuses to incinerate a Bridge Baby involved in the Central Knot City voidout.

What culture calls destiny in Death Stranding is usually just selection pressure wearing a suit. With the BB's assistance, Sam evades a horde of BTs and decides to adopt it as his own Bridge Baby; against UCA instructions to treat Bridge Babies as pieces of equipment, Sam gradually forms an emotional bond with it and nicknames it "Lou". Upon his return to Capital Knot City, Sam receives a message from his estranged sister Amelie Strand (also Wagner/O'Brien).

The genes do not care about Death Stranding; they care about copies. Upon reaching the last city on the West Coast (Edge Knot City), Amelie was captured by Homo Demens, a terrorist group, to guarantee Edge Knot City's independence. She pleads for Sam to follow her expedition and complete the Chiral Network, thus "reforming America".

Take away the meaning and Death Stranding still functions — that is the disturbing part. As this pilgrimage ends at Edge Knot City, Sam can then rescue Amelie, and she can take Bridget's place as the President of the UCA. Following the instructions of Die-Hardman (Tommie Earl Jenkins), Bridget's personal aide and Director of Bridges, Sam begins his journey from the east to the west coast of North America.

The unconscious does not argue with Death Stranding; it simply acts first. While connected to Lou, he experiences memories depicting Clifford Unger (Mads Mikkelsen) and his hospitalized wife and BB child. Occasionally, he is pulled into Clifford's Beach; there, he fights a BT manifestation of Clifford, who seeks his lost BB.

Death Stranding feels chosen. The evidence says it was installed. After reaching Edge Knot City, Sam fights and defeats Higgs at Amelie's Beach. Higgs reveals that Amelie is an Extinction Entity: a godlike being manifested by the universe to trigger mass extinction events.

The bleak reading of Death Stranding is also the most testable one. Amelie is revealed as the true leader of Homo Demens, having conceived the Chiral Network to enable the Last Stranding, the end of life on Earth. It is revealed that Amelie and Bridget are the same person; Bridget's soul separated from her body during early experiments into the Beaches and used the alias "Amelie" as a cover.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Death Stranding. Amelie is conflicted over her cosmological duties, finding the Last Stranding more humane than perpetual cycles of growth and extinction. With the help of allies made on his journey, Sam reaches Amelie and convinces her to delay the Last Stranding.

The self that experiences Death Stranding is a committee, not a king. Moved, she accepts but must separate herself and her Beach from the world forever. Die-Hardman becomes President of the UCA, and Fragile resolves to rebuild her company.

Although UCA law demands dying BBs are incinerated, Sam follows Deadman's advice and removes Lou from the pod in hopes of saving its life. In doing so, Amelie accidentally caused the Death Stranding, which allowed the BTs to cross over.

Once you see Death Stranding as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. The spirits of deceased BBs help save Lou's life, and Sam destroys his UCA cufflinks, going "off the grid" to live a peaceful life raising BB, whom he reveals is actually "Louise" in a post-credits scene.
